A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same recursive diffusion-model study despite retitling and reformatting. Their text, equations, ten figures, and Appendices A–G are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian-mixture simulations and Fashion-MNIST/CIFAR-10 experiments, including divergence estimates, observability measurements, and generated samples in Figures 1–10 and Appendix G.

after.justification: v2 retains the original simulations and image experiments, including their measured outcomes and generated samples in Figures 1–10 and Appendix G.

M1.justification: The real/synthetic mixture recursion, score-learning objectives, and reverse-diffusion sampling procedures are unchanged. The added linear-Gaussian example explains observability without introducing a new training or inference method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same five-component, 10-dimensional Gaussian mixture, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10, with the same recursive-training and controlled-perturbation scenarios.

E2.justification: The learned-score versus ideal/ablated-score controls and aligned, random, and time-only perturbation comparisons are retained. Newly cited theoretical works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix G retains the experimental protocols: 100,000 GMM training samples, 20 generations, and 500 sampling steps; the image training budgets, DDPM sampling, and feature-space divergence estimation also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The controlled perturbation study, generation-specific score-replacement ablations, memory-contribution analyses, and qualitative sample comparisons are unchanged. The new linear-Gaussian illustration is a theoretical derivation, not an additional empirical analysis.

E5.justification: The GMM experiments still report ten independent runs per configuration. The existing standard-deviation shading and uncertainty descriptions are retained, without new run counts, confidence intervals, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Figures 1–10 retain identical graphics and reported results; Appendix G's findings are unchanged, including CIFAR-10 observability around 0.25–0.35. The new discussion of Figure 3's initial discrepancy interprets existing evidence.

T1.justification: Proposition 4.1(i) removes v1's assertion that non-summable score errors prevent divergence from converging to zero; it now guarantees only non-summability of divergence. Theorem 3.5, formerly 3.4, explicitly requires uniformly positive observability for its equivalence statement. Section 3.2 also adds a linear-Gaussian observability derivation and sufficient-condition reasoning for A3. These substantively revise the scope and mathematical support of central results, although most appendix proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The main contribution now ties nonvanishing divergence to a positive score-error floor, replacing v1's broader non-summability claim. The introduction also withdraws the assertion that theoretical diffusion-retraining analyses are absent and positions this work as complementary, architecture-agnostic lower-bound analysis.

C2.justification: v2 explains that bounded score errors suffice for A3 but do not imply A4, interprets Figure 3's first-generation mismatch as a transient, and expands the argument for neglecting initialization bias at large diffusion horizons. These refine applicability and interpretation of the retained analysis.

D1.justification: Appendix G retains the same architectures, KDE bandwidth, optimizers, hyperparameters, sampling procedures, and metric-estimation details. No new implementation release or code/data-access information is provided.

R1.justification: The introduction adds Fu et al. (2024) and Cui et al. (2026) as existing architecture-specific theory and contrasts their upper bounds with this work's approach, substantially revising the stated research gap. Lewis et al. (2025) and Bakry and Emery (1985) are also added, while Chen et al. (2025) is removed. Duplicate-reference consolidation does not constitute removal of distinct works.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title, expands the abstract and explanatory passages, standardizes mathematical notation, revises Appendix A/B.1 exposition, corrects wording, and adds acknowledgements. The main Sections 1–5 and Appendices A–G retain their overall organization.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch from single-column to two-column layout, substantially reflowing equations, captions, and figure placement, with Figures 1 and 2 reduced to column width. All ten figure graphics are retained; the appendices remain single-column.

improvement.justification: v2 improves the precision of the existing theory by removing the overly broad nonconvergence claim in Proposition 4.1 and explicitly qualifying the equivalence in Theorem 3.5. Acknowledging prior theoretical work and explaining assumptions also improve credibility and readability. These are useful corrections and clarifications within a largely retained theoretical framework and empirical record.
